title: Early-Life Famine Exposure and Risk of Cardiovascular Diseases in Later Life: Findings From the REACTION Study.
ehr_evidence: The data source was the REACTION (Risk Evaluation of Cancers in Chinese Diabetic Individuals: A Longitudinal) Study, a nationwide prospective observational cohort in which 'all questionnaire data collection and anthropometric measurements were performed by trained staff according to a standard protocol at local health stations or community clinics,' and CVD outcomes were collected via interviewer-assisted self-reported questionnaire rather than electronic health records.
summary: In this cross-sectional analysis of 234,219 Chinese community-dwelling adults aged 40+ from the REACTION cohort, early-life famine exposure (fetal, childhood, and adolescent) was associated with significantly increased risks of total CVD, myocardial infarction, stroke, and coronary heart disease.
key_findings: In the multivariable-adjusted model, fetal famine exposure was associated with ORs (95% CI) of 1.35 (1.20–1.52) for total CVD, 1.59 (1.08–2.35) for MI, 1.40 (1.11–1.78) for stroke, and 1.44 (1.26–1.65) for CHD.
Childhood famine exposure was associated with ORs of 1.59 (1.40–1.81) for total CVD, 2.20 (1.52–3.20) for MI, 1.82 (1.45–2.28) for stroke, and 1.80 (1.56–2.09) for CHD.
Adolescent famine exposure was associated with ORs of 1.52 (1.27–1.81) for total CVD, 2.07 (1.28–3.35) for MI, 1.92 (1.42–2.58) for stroke, and 1.83 (1.50–2.24) for CHD.

Individuals in severely affected famine areas had significantly increased risks of total CVD compared with less severely affected areas across all three exposure groups (e.g., total CVD OR 1.84, 95% CI 1.52–2.22).
The association between famine exposure and CVD was partly mediated via metabolic syndrome and was stronger in women (all P for interaction <0.05).
captured_features: Birth date used to classify famine exposure period (fetal, childhood, adolescent)
Lipid profiles (triglycerides, HDL-C, LDL-C, total cholesterol)
Serum creatinine, fasting insulin, glycated hemoglobin
Self-reported total CVD, MI, stroke, and CHD
study_design: Cross-sectional analysis of baseline data from a nationwide prospective cohort
data_source_type: Other (population-based prospective cohort with baseline survey, clinical examination, and biospecimen data)
population: 234,219 Chinese community-dwelling adults aged 40 years or older from 25 centers across mainland China (baseline survey 2011–2012)
limitations: CVD outcomes were self-reported, leading to recall bias.
Cross-sectional design prevented assessment of CVD incidence and causal inference.
Exposure classified by birth date, risking misclassification because the famine had no definitive start/end.
Famine severity indexed by regional excess death rate did not fully account for other death-related factors.
Residual age differences among exposure groups remained despite sensitivity analyses.
Birth weight was not collected, limiting control of its influence.
No early-life lifestyle data were available.
